title: Service station burns 1968
description: At around 9 a.m. on Saturday, January 20, 1968, while Blaine Hallett and his men were working on the garage floor, an explosion occurred at the Irving station. It is believed that leaking gas may have been ignited by the furnace. Immediately, flames engulfed the building, leaving no time to retrieve account books, cash, or any belongings. The explosion blew out the windows and doors, sending them about fifty feet from the structure. Losses included cash, cheques, credit card receipts, equipment, tires, parts, and tools, totalling more than $15,000. Fortunately, Blaine had one cheque in his pocket, a $1,000 government payment for school bus repairs and servicing.
